prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Cross-tab · Regional sales (language en).
Grid: 7 columns × 5 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Region" · longest unbreakable word 57px · one-line width 195px
  col 2: header "Jan" · longest unbreakable word 38px · one-line width 38px
  col 3: header "Feb" · longest unbreakable word 38px · one-line width 38px
  col 4: header "Mar" · longest unbreakable word 38px · one-line width 38px
  col 5: header "Apr" · longest unbreakable word 38px · one-line width 38px
  col 6: header "May" · longest unbreakable word 38px · one-line width 38px
  col 7: header "Jun" · longest unbreakable word 38px · one-line width 38px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 490px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 489px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 490px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"Compare monthly sales across regions from January through June.","reading":"Readers scan across each row to follow a region over time and down each month to compare regions.","groups":["January–June are parallel monthly measures and should have consistent widths.","The region column identifies each row and needs enough space for recognizable labels."],"keep_intact":["Month names","Sales figures, including thousands separators","Individual words in region names"],"may_wrap":["Multiword region names may wrap at spaces; the long Europe, Middle East & Africa label is the main candidate."]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[135,59,59,59,59,59,59],"idea":"Give the region labels the most space available while keeping all six monthly values intact in equal-width columns."},{"name":"B","widths":[111,63,63,63,63,63,63],"idea":"Balance moderate wrapping of region labels with a little more breathing room for each month."},{"name":"C","widths":[78,68,68,68,68,68,68],"idea":"Give the monthly comparisons generous, equal space while allowing region labels to wrap across several lines without breaking words."}]}
